observations.semantic_recognizability: All three-quarter, profile, and detail production renders read as an open-frame computer desk; separate monitors remain on the top.
observations.silhouette_quality: The thin top and exposed support frame correct the heavy box shape, but four independent posts still differ from the reference's two standing-desk end frames.
observations.proportion: Godot measured 66 x 30 x 30 inches; the top reads thin relative to the full width and height.
observations.geometric_detail: The close render shows a beveled top, narrow legs, collars, rubber feet, cross supports, and cable tray. The base lacks depth-spanning T feet.
observations.material_realism: The tabletop has one visible specular point but reads mostly as flat dark material rather than reflective smoked glass.
observations.surface_variation: The glass, dark frame, and steel collars separate at close range, though the desktop remains nearly uniform.
observations.close_up_quality: The profile and detail views expose the thin edge and support rails; nearby monitor and chair props remain present in the real room.
observations.gameplay_readability: The table surface and independent monitor silhouettes remain readable in the production room.
observations.scale_fidelity: The technical report confirms exact 66 x 30 x 30-inch mesh bounds and floor contact.
observations.art_direction_fit: The cleaner frame is compatible with the room's stylized look and matches the modern workstation better than v1.
observations.technical_integration: Godot imported 23 meshes and 23 surfaces; the stable desk resolver selected desk-v002 with no fallback and technical validation passed.
observations.source_resemblance: Sample (2) has two rectangular standing-desk columns and broad T-shaped feet; v2 has four narrow cylindrical posts and no full-width feet.

defects: The four-post silhouette does not match the two end-frame standing-desk supports visible in Sample (2).
The dark tabletop gets only a small localized highlight and still reads more like painted metal than smoked glass.
The feet do not create the characteristic depth-spanning T base shown in the reference.
likely_causes: The v2 recipe describes four narrow tubular legs and levelers instead of two structural end frames with transverse feet.
The uniformly dark opaque top has limited broad reflection cues in the current room lighting.
next_action_hypothesis: Change the construction to a standing-desk-specific double T-frame: two rectangular graphite lift columns, one broad floor-level foot per end spanning nearly the full desk depth, and a rear crossbar under the smoked-glass top. Increase the glass's controlled specular and clearcoat response while keeping its dark tint. Keep bounds and all RoomDefinition geometry unchanged.
incumbent_comparison: Better than desk-v001 on silhouette, proportion, surface variation, close-up quality, art-direction fit, and source resemblance; current best-so-far candidate, still below the source-resemblance and material gates.
